battle.name: 維京人第二次入侵愛爾蘭
battle.brief: 914年伊瑪率北歐大軍再入愛爾蘭，焚莫維爾修院、攻陷都柏林Dubh Linn，916年殺克朗納德院長，920年兵焚利費河畔而退。卡面希臘重步兵成於公元前五世紀，絕跡逾千年；方陣互助的原理在Dubh Linn城下的盾牆裡換副面孔重現——盾牆正面比個人結實，正是立陣決勝的憑依。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries:
維京一方並非國家軍隊，而是北歐貴族帶領的遠征私兵聯盟。914年率隊登陸愛爾蘭的是Ímar（伊瑪，英語作 Ivar the Boneless，綽號「無骨者」），愛爾蘭編年史稱他為「薩克遜人的王」；同行者多為他的兄弟與親族首領，其中Óláfr與Gofraid的名字在後來的編年史中常與他並列。這支隊伍的成員來自丹麥、挪威與瑞典西岸的沿海，按長船分隊，各隊的首領就是自己的指揮官，戰與不戰的決定以及戰利品的分配，都在首領的會議上落定。船隊攜帶人、馬、武器與供應品，目標是奪取修道院的金屬與白銀、取得立足之地與航路據點，而不是征服全島。Ímar於914年佔據利費河出海口的沼澤地Dubh Linn（黑池，即都柏林），在島上的諾伊欣島與對岸之間架起棧橋，把一個原本的漁村變成北歐人在西海的據點與跳板；這座聚落後來成為諾斯人王國的都城。
愛爾蘭一方也不是一個國家。島上由數十個小王分據，各王依氏族與地區劃分勢力，高王只是諸王之首，沒有常備軍、常備倉廩，也沒有足以長期支應的稅基。每次出征都由各王臨時集結兵力，兵員自備武器、自備口糧，作戰一結束即散歸田里。編年史記錄戰事因此多為「某某王在某地與薩克遜人交戰」，而不是一次有統一計畫的會戰。與維京人直接對抗的愛爾蘭領袖之中，高王Máel Sechnaill mac Domnaill（梅爾・謝赫奈爾・麥克・多姆納爾）自916年起先後擔任高王，是這場戰爭中唯一三度在野戰中擊敗維京大軍的人；黎恩斯特的諸王控制著都柏林所在的芬尼與黎恩斯特地界，奧爾福德人、布雷尼人等部族也各以地區兵力參戰。愛爾蘭的教會屬羅馬教會，修道院同時是財富中心、地方社會的組織者與抵抗的節點，戰時教區與世俗王權的關係相當緊密。除了修道院網絡與遠方的教會援助，這場戰爭在愛爾蘭編年史中就是愛爾蘭人與「薩克遜人」的對抗，雙方之外並無成形的聯軍。
countriesEn: The Viking side was not a national army but a war-band confederation led by the magnates of the North. The man who landed in Ireland in 914 was Ímar, Ivar the Boneless in English, whom the Irish annals call king of the Saxons; his companions were mostly his brothers and the chiefs of his kin, and the names Óláfr and Gofraid are the ones the later annals repeatedly place beside him. The men came from the coasts of Denmark, Norway and western Sweden and were organised by longship, each crew's leader being his own commander, and both the decision to fight and the division of the spoils were settled in a council of these chiefs. The fleet carried men, horses, weapons and supplies, and its aim was to take the metal and silver of the monasteries, to obtain land and a station on the sea route, not to conquer the whole island. In 914 Ímar seized Dubh Linn, the Black Pool, that is Dublin, a marshy site at the mouth of the Liffey, and laid a timber causeway between the island of Nóibhín and the mainland, turning what had been a fishing settlement into a Northman's foothold and springboard in the western sea; that settlement was later to become the capital of the Norse kingdom. The Irish side was not a state either. The island was divided among several dozen petty kings, each holding a share of it by clan and district; the High King was only the first among kings, with no standing army, no standing storehouses and no tax base capable of sustaining a campaign. Every muster was improvised: the kings brought their own men, who brought their own weapons and their own food, and once the fighting was over the army dissolved back into the fields. That is why the annals record such campaigns as one king or another fighting the Saxons at such and such a place, rather than as battles with a unified plan. Among the Irish leaders who faced the Vikings directly, the High King Máel Sechnaill mac Domnaill, first raised to the kingship in 916, was the one man who defeated a Viking host in open field three times over; the kings of Leinster held the ground on which Dublin lay, and the Uí Mórdha and the Bréifne brought their district levies to the same war. The Irish Church belonged to Rome, and the monasteries were at once centres of wealth, organisers of local society and nodes of resistance, and the ties between the bishops and the secular kings were close in wartime. Apart from the monastic network and distant support from the Church, the war as the Irish annals frame it was a confrontation between the Irish and the Saxons, with no formed coalition on either side.
people:
留下姓名的關鍵人物分屬兩邊，而愛爾蘭一邊的記錄遠為完整，因為編年史是由取勝的一方寫下的。
維京方面的主腦是Ímar。914年他率船隊抵達愛爾蘭，先在Donegal的莫維爾（Moville）洗劫修院，再南下攻取Dubh Linn；915年肯尼之敗後他退保都柏林，918年被愛爾蘭人與都柏林居民聯手逐出，919年又率大軍回來包圍都柏林，920年在利費河畔的決戰中失去大部分船隻，僅以殘部退回北方。此後他在英格蘭東部重新站穩腳跟，約920年代回到英格蘭活動，925年死於東英格蘭；後來北約克蘭那座俗稱「伊瓦爾王墓」的巨大石塚，學界常認為可能就是他的墳墓。他的兄弟Óláfr與Gofraid常被認為與他同來；917年島橋之戰中被愛爾蘭人殺死的諾斯王，就是編年史所記的Gofraid。Sigtrygg（西格特里格），後世加號稱「絲綢鬍子」的那一位，在918年之後成為都柏林之王，執政到1036年；在位期間都柏林王國完成制度化，重建城防、鑄造以自己命名的芬尼錢幣，並在1030年前後接受基督教洗禮。他的兒子奧拉夫・庫蘭（Amlaíb Cuarán）後來兼任約克王與都柏林王，說明都柏林從此嵌在北歐諸王的政治網絡之中。
愛爾蘭方面，核心是梅爾・謝赫奈爾・麥克・多姆納爾。他以高王的身份在肯尼、島橋與都柏林一役三度擊敗北歐大軍，而且不把戰果停在口頭上：戰後他推動修院加建城防與石造圓塔，又逐步恢復對愛爾蘭海航運的掌控。黎恩斯特的諸王與都柏林的爭端，也把他的軍隊拉進戰場。教會方面最著名的一個名字是弗蘭・費納（Flann Fina），克朗納德（Clonard）修院的院長，編年史記他於916年在都柏林被維京人所殺；他的名字說明戰爭已經從河道打到修院的門內。此外，愛爾蘭詩人與修士在這一時期寫下的文字，例如抄成於九至十世紀之交、保存現存最古老古愛爾蘭語詩歌的聖加爾普里西安抄本，為這場戰爭留下了另一種證據：戰士接戰前所誦的戰鬥咒語，以及隨軍修道士記下的戰況。
peopleEn: The names that survive fall on two sides, and the record on the Irish side is far fuller, because the annals were written by the winners. The mastermind on the Viking side was Ímar. In 914 he brought his fleet to Ireland, plundered the monastery at Moville in Donegal, and moved south to take Dubh Linn; after the defeat at Confey in 915 he fell back on Dublin, was driven out in 918 by the Irish together with the people of Dublin itself, returned with a great army in 919 to besiege the town, and in the battle by the Liffey in 920 lost most of his ships, escaping north with the remnant. He afterwards re-established himself in eastern England, was back in England in the 920s, and died in East Anglia in 925; the great stone mound in North Yorkshire long known as Ivar's Boneless is often taken by scholars to be his grave. His brothers Óláfr and Gofraid are generally held to have come with him, and the Norse king slain by the Irish at the Battle of Islandbridge in 917 is the Gofraid of the annals. Sigtrygg, the one who was afterwards given the by-name Silkbeard, became king of Dublin after 918 and ruled until 1036; in his reign the Dublin kingdom was institutionalised, its defences rebuilt, its own pennies struck under his name, and he accepted Christian baptism around 1030. His son Amlaíb Cuarán was later king of York as well as king of Dublin, which shows that Dublin from that point was set inside the political network of the Norse kings. On the Irish side the central figure is Máel Sechnaill mac Domnaill. As High King he defeated the northern host in the field at Confey, at Islandbridge and at Dublin, and he did not stop at the boast: in the years after the war he pushed the monasteries to add fortifications and stone round towers, and he gradually recovered control of the shipping on the Irish Sea. The disputes of the kings of Leinster over Dublin likewise dragged his levies into the field. The best known name on the ecclesiastical side is Flann Fina, abbot of the monastery at Clonard, whom the annals record as killed by the Vikings at Dublin in 916; his name shows that the war had been carried from the river up to the door of the monastery. A second kind of evidence comes from the words of Irish poets and monks in these years, such as the St Gall Priscian, copied at the turn of the ninth and tenth centuries and preserving the oldest surviving poem in Old Irish: the battle charms the warriors recited before contact, and the reports of the monks who marched with them.
kits:
先把最容易被誤讀的事說清楚：卡面上的希臘重步兵（hoplite）並沒有出現在914年的愛爾蘭。hoplite是公元前五世紀至前四世紀希臘城邦的產物——青銅頭盔、青銅或亞麻布胸甲、圓盾（aspis）、長矛與一把短劍，配上要求單手扶矛、身體收攏在盾後的進攻動作；到公元914年，這個兵種早已絕跡一千四百年有奇，像樣的方陣會戰也要數百年前，馬其頓方陣與塞琉古方陣都已不成體系。但把這張卡放進這場戰爭並非毫無道理：方陣最耐用的那一部分——盾牌接成人牆、正面比任何個人都結實——以「盾牆」的形式活到中世紀，並且在Dubh Linn城下的每一次交鋒裡重新出現。
維京人實際攜帶的裝備以雙刃直劍、闊刃斧與長矛為主，配以圓盾與盾翼形長盾（kite shield），鎧甲是歐洲當時最紮實的一批：鎖子甲上衣配皮甲襯裡；頭盔仍以皮或青銅為主，要到十至十一世紀才出現鼻護盔。弓在維京軍中只是輔助，主要的搏鬥發生在盾牆與斧、劍之間。維京遠征隊另一項決定性資源是馬：九至十世紀的北歐人是歐洲最早成建制的重騎兵群之一，可以騎馬快速掠奪、騎馬追擊，也可以下馬列盾牆作戰。愛爾蘭軍隊幾乎全為步兵，裝備是長短矛、單刃長柄斧、以皮革包覆並加鐵釘的圓盾，皮甲數量有限，金屬甲胄在當時的愛爾蘭極為罕見；投射武器以投石與標槍為數，主要用於騷擾而非壓制。雙方的刀劍都短於維京劍，愛爾蘭劍形更接近柳葉形，配以圓形或淺盤形護手，寬而薄，適合劈砍而非刺擊。
攻城與運輸方面，這場戰爭留下的記載有限，考古才是主要線索：914年前後的都柏林城防以木柵、土壘與池沼地形的天然屏障為主，橫越利費河的棧橋把島上的聚落與陸地相連，一旦棧橋被切斷，島上的守軍就成孤軍；1970年代在利費河下游的考古更發現以木樁封鎖水道的設施痕跡。維京人帶有攻船與粗木撞柱，但沒有留下可考的攻城塔。船隊本身分兩種：吃水淺的長船供戰士划槍作戰，寬腹的貨船載運馬匹、穀物與戰利品；編年史不記船數，通行推測此次遠征的船隊在數十艘之譜。
kitsEn: First the thing most easily misread must be said plainly: the Greek hoplite on the card did not appear in Ireland in 914. The hoplite was a product of the Greek city states of the fifth and fourth centuries BC: a bronze helmet, a bronze or linen cuirass, a round shield, the aspis, a long spear and a short sword, worn with a style of advance that required the spear to be held one-handed and the body to be kept close behind the shield. By AD 914 that arm had been extinct for something like fourteen hundred years, and the last respectable battle of a phalanx lay centuries further back still, with the Macedonian and Seleucid phalanxes long since dissolved. Yet the card is not idle in this war. The part of the phalanx that proved most durable, the shields locked into a wall so that the front of the host was stronger than any man in it, survived into the Middle Ages under the name of the shield wall, and turned up again at every clash below the walls of Dubh Linn. What the Vikings actually carried was axe, spear and double-edged straight sword, with round shields and kite-shaped shields, and armour that was among the best in contemporary Europe: mail shirts worn over leather, with helmets still of leather or bronze, the nasal helm belonging to the tenth and eleventh centuries. The bow was a secondary arm in the Viking host, for the real business of the shield wall was fought with axe and sword. The other decisive resource of the Viking expedition was the horse: the Northmen of the ninth and tenth centuries were among the first organised heavy cavalry in Europe, able to ride out to plunder at speed, to ride down a fugitive, and to dismount and stand in a shield wall. The Irish army was almost entirely infantry, armed with spears both long and short, single-bitted axes on long hafts, and round shields of hide over wood studded with iron; leather armour was limited and metal harness was extremely rare in contemporary Ireland, and the missile weapons, slings and javelins, were used for harassment rather than for shock. The swords on both sides were shorter than the Viking sword, the Irish blade tending towards a willow-leaf shape with a round or dish-shaped guard, broad and thin, and made to cut rather than to thrust. On siege and transport the written record of this war is thin and archaeology is the main line of evidence. The defences of Dublin of that time consisted of timber palisades, earthen banks and the natural barrier of the marshy ground, with a timber causeway across the Liffey linking the settlement on the island to the mainland; cut the causeway and the garrison on the island was isolated. Excavations of the 1970s on the lower Liffey have further turned up traces of a barrier of timber piles closing a water channel. The Vikings brought assault boats and heavy timber rams, but no identifiable siege tower survives. Their fleet came in two kinds: shallow-draught longships for the warriors to row and fight from, and broad-bellied cargo ships for horses, grain and plunder. The annals give no number of ships, and the usual estimate for this expedition is a fleet of several tens of vessels.
tactics:
維京人在愛爾蘭的整套打法，可以歸成一句話：不正面接戰，先取據點，再靠速度與突襲把戰局拖成游擊。
第一步是登陸與掠奪。914年的船隊先在Donegal上岸洗劫莫維爾修院，把修院積存的金屬與白銀裝船，再沿海岸南下直取Dubh Linn。這是典型的北歐遠征邏輯：修道院在九至十世紀的愛爾蘭是最大的財富集中地之一，修院守備薄弱、財物外運不便，正是最划算的目標；修院既是誘餌，也是愛爾蘭人的抵抗節點，劫掠之後隨之而來的必然是加固。
第二步是據點化。Dubh Linn在利費河出海處，天然避風，島與陸地之間退潮可行、漲潮即隔絕，橫跨水道的木棧橋是唯一的通道。維京人佔下這裡，等於在愛爾蘭東岸插上一枚釘子：往北可通蘇格蘭與斯堪的納維亞，往東可回英格蘭，而愛爾蘭修院靠海路與英格蘭、歐陸往來的商船必須經過這片水域。
第三步是避免主力會戰。維京人盡量以小股戰團分頭劫掠，遇上有利可圖的目標才集結，並且經常在愛爾蘭諸王集結完畢之前退走。917年與920年的兩次失利，都發生在愛爾蘭人已把兵力集結完畢、並且選好地點的時候——肯尼與島橋都是愛爾蘭人選的戰場，島橋更是利費河上一處狹窄的河段，維京人一旦湧上橋面與岸頭，數量上的優勢便被地形抵銷。
第四步是盾牆。915年之後的戰鬥，愛爾蘭步兵在編年史與詩篇裡被描述為結「盾牆」：盾牌互相搭接成線，前排以矛支撐，後排以短兵器擊打伸入的敵手。這正是卡面hoplite那個核心原理的隔代再現：方陣講究的從來不是單兵武藝，而是把盾接起來、讓正面變成一道沒有弱點的牆。維京軍同樣排盾牆，以鎖子甲與斧劍在前面頂住，把雙手闊刃斧當破陣工具；雙方的差別在於維京軍有馬可以脫離接戰，愛爾蘭人沒有。
第五步是攻城與撤退的混合。918年維京人退出Dubh Linn，是愛爾蘭人與都柏林居民聯合起來的結果；919年Ímar回來之後包圍都柏林、洗掠基爾代爾等修院，最終在920年再戰一場，Dubh Linn的城與泊在河口的船隊同歸於盡，殘餘船隻帶著人離去。這場戰爭的實際收場，是打散維京大軍，而非摧毀都柏林的北歐聚落。
tacticsEn: The whole Viking method in Ireland can be reduced to one sentence: do not accept a general engagement, take the point first, and then use speed and surprise to turn the war into a running skirmish. The first step was landing and plunder. The fleet of 914 came ashore in Donegal, stripped the monastery at Moville, loaded the metal and silver the abbey had hoarded into the ships, and moved south along the coast to take Dubh Linn directly. This is the classic logic of the Norse expedition: the monastery was one of the greatest concentrations of wealth in the Ireland of the ninth and tenth centuries, thinly defended and awkward to move goods out of, which made it the most profitable target available; and because the monastery was at once the bait and the node of Irish resistance, every raid on it was followed by an increase in fortification. The second step was turning the prize into a base. Dubh Linn lay where the Liffey meets the sea, sheltered by nature, with the island and the mainland crossable at low tide and cut off at high, and the timber causeway over the water the only link between them. By taking it the Vikings drove a spike into the eastern coast of Ireland: north to Scotland and Scandinavia, east back to England, while the ships that carried the trade of the Irish monasteries to England and to the Continent had to pass through these waters. The third step was refusing the general engagement. The Vikings plundered in small war bands, concentrated only when a worthwhile target appeared, and as a rule withdrew before the Irish kings had finished mustering. Both disasters of 917 and 920 came after the Irish had completed their muster and chosen their ground. Confey and Islandbridge were both Irish choices, and Islandbridge in particular is a narrow reach of the Liffey: once the Vikings were crowded onto the bridge and onto the bank, their advantage in numbers was cancelled out by the ground. The fourth step was the shield wall. In the fighting after 915 the Irish infantry are described in the annals and in the poems as forming a wall of shields, shields overlapped into a single line, the front rank braced behind spears, the rear striking at the enemy who forced their hands in with short weapons. This is the central principle of the hoplite on the card, appearing a thousand years later in another form. What the phalanx had always insisted on was not individual skill but the locking of shields into a front with no weak place in it. The Vikings stood in a wall of shields too, holding the front with mail, axe and sword and using the two-handed broad-bladed axe as a breaching tool; the difference between the two armies was that the Vikings had horses and could break off, and the Irish did not. The fifth step was a mixture of siege and withdrawal. The Vikings left Dublin in 918 as a result of the Irish and the townspeople of Dublin acting together; Ímar came back in 919, besieged the town, and stripped the churches at Kildare and elsewhere; in 920 there was one more pitched battle, and the town of Dubh Linn and the fleet lying off the river were destroyed together, the surviving ships carrying men away. The practical outcome of the war was the breaking up of the Viking host, not the destruction of the Northman's settlement at Dublin.
data:
可核對的數字分三類。
第一類是編年史的逐年記載，這是本場戰爭最硬的一條時間線：914年大軍抵達、洗劫莫維爾、Dubh Linn淪陷；915年高王在肯尼（Cenn Cona，位於今米斯郡）擊敗維京軍，Dubh Linn隨後被焚，至於火是撤退時自焚還是愛爾蘭人所放，各家解讀不一；916年維京人回攻都柏林，克朗納德修院院長弗蘭・費納死於城中；917年島橋（Islandbridge）之戰，愛爾蘭人擊敗維京軍並殺死諾斯王Gofraid；918年高王與都柏林居民聯手逼走Ímar；919年Ímar率大軍返回，包圍都柏林；919至920年間，基爾代爾（Cill Mhaille）等修院被洗掠；920年決戰於都柏林，Dubh Linn城與維京艦隊俱燒，Ímar僅以殘船遁走。愛爾蘭編年史只標年份不標月份，通行說法把大軍抵岸與第一次交鋒放在該年的春末夏初。
第二類是考古數字。Dubh Linn的聚落遺址自1960年代起被系統發掘，1980至1990年代在利費河北岸Wood Quay一帶的工地出土大批九至十世紀的層位：長屋的柱洞、地下窖穴、鐵器與木工工具、錢幣，以及被棄置或掩埋的骨骸，其中以頭顱與軀幹分離的葬式最為學界議論，一般認為與信仰轉變時期的處置方式有關。錢幣方面，都柏林自十世紀起鑄造芬尼，體系主要承襲英格蘭與愛爾蘭本土的錢制，出土數以萬計，屬西歐最早的一批本國鑄幣。聚落規模在十世紀初仍是數百人量級，範圍不過利費河北岸黑池一帶的數百公尺，十一世紀之後才隨城防與市集而擴張。
第三類是必須打折扣的推估。遠征船隊的船數、每次會戰的兵力，編年史一概不載，通行說法只說「大軍」與「數十艘船」；九至十世紀愛爾蘭的人口估計多在百萬上下，說法分歧頗大；都柏林的諾斯人王國延續到十二世紀末才告終，其盛時人口通常估在數千人。至於雙方的戰鬥傷亡，沒有任何可靠記載，精確數字都屬後人推想，不應引用。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is the year-by-year record of the annals, which is the hardest timeline this war possesses. In 914 the host arrived, stripped Moville, and Dubh Linn fell. In 915 the High King defeated the Vikings at Confey, Cenn Cona in what is now County Meath, and Dublin was burned afterwards, though whether the fire was the Vikings' own as they left or the Irish's is read differently by different annalists. In 916 the Vikings struck back at Dublin and Flann Fina, abbot of Clonard, was killed in the town. In 917 came the battle of Islandbridge, in which the Irish defeated the Viking host and slew their king Gofraid. In 918 the High King and the people of Dublin together drove Ímar out. In 919 Ímar returned with a great army and besieged Dublin, and between 919 and 920 the churches at Kildare, Cill Mhaille, and elsewhere were plundered. In 920 the decisive action was fought at Dublin itself, the town of Dubh Linn and the Viking fleet were burned, and Ímar escaped with the remnant of his ships. The Irish annals mark the year but not the month; the received view places the landing and the first fighting in the late spring and early summer of that year. The second class is archaeological. The settlement site of Dubh Linn has been systematically excavated since the 1960s, and building work on the north bank of the Liffey at Wood Quay in the 1980s and 1990s produced large quantities of ninth and tenth century material: postholes of longhouses, underground cellars, iron and woodworking tools, coins, and bone that was either discarded or buried, of which the decapitated burials have provoked the most discussion, being generally read as a practice of the period of religious change. In the matter of money, Dublin began striking its own pennies in the tenth century, on a system largely inherited from the coinages of England and of Ireland itself; they have been found by the tens of thousands, and they belong to the earliest native coinages of north-western Europe. The settlement was still of the order of a few hundred people in the early tenth century and covered only a few hundred metres along the north bank of the Liffey by the Black Pool, expanding only later in the eleventh century with the defences and the market. The third class is estimate, and has to be discounted. The annals give neither the number of ships in the expedition nor the strength of any engagement, saying only of a great host and of several tens of ships. The population of Ireland in the ninth and tenth centuries is commonly put in the region of a million, with wide disagreement between estimates. The Norse kingdom of Dublin lasted until the end of the twelfth century, and its population at its height is usually estimated in the thousands. As for the losses of the fighting, no reliable figure survives at all, and any exact number is later speculation that should not be quoted.
cause:
打起來有四層原因，一層推一層。
最外一層是愛爾蘭這邊的錢財結構。九至十世紀的愛爾蘭修道院是全島最大的財富集中地：黃銅器皿、飾物、聖物、藏書，還有向外界換來的貴金屬，樣樣都要運出島去。修院防備薄弱、財物外運不便，落在北歐人眼中，這是天下最容易取用的財源。修院同時是地方社會的組織者，是各氏族與教區的紐帶，也是愛爾蘭人抵抗的節點；它既招來劫掠，也促成防禦的加強。
第二層是北歐那邊的推力。八至九世紀的北歐經歷人口增長與土地壓力，維京遠征從零星掠奪轉為有組織的殖遷；而西邊的英格蘭在877至878年被艾爾弗雷德大帝及諸王聯軍擊敗之後，英格蘭的基地與分贓管道被切斷，殘餘的北歐戰團被推向更西的海面，愛爾蘭是他們能夠找到的最近一塊跳板。914年的入侵因此不是孤立的搶掠，而是被逐出英格蘭之後的重新部署。
第三層是愛爾蘭內部的結構性弱點。島上沒有中央軍隊，各小王只在名義上服從高王，兵員與裝備都靠各部自備，臨時集結往往要拖上數週；高王的權威要靠一次次的共同勝利來維持，一旦敗一次，號召力便受損。維京人正是利用這個時間差：總在愛爾蘭人還沒集合完畢時打，打完就走。
第四層是地緣。Dubh Linn在利費河出海口，是愛爾蘭東岸唯一天然避風、又能控制愛爾蘭海航路的泊地，佔下它，維京人就有了一個可以年年收取過路收益的基地；而愛爾蘭的海外關係——教會、貿易、典籍——都要經過這片海域。於是「拿下Dubh Linn」成為雙方都知道值得付出的目標。
causeEn: There are four layers of cause, each resting on the one below it. The outermost layer is the structure of wealth on the Irish side. In the Ireland of the ninth and tenth centuries the monasteries were the largest concentrations of wealth on the island: brass, ornaments, relics, libraries and precious metal bought from outside all had to be carried off the island. Poorly defended and awkward to move goods out of, the monasteries offered the Northmen the most easily taken wealth in the world. At the same time they were the organisers of local society, the tie between clans and dioceses, and the nodes of Irish resistance, so that what invited the raid also brought about the strengthening of the defences. The second layer is the pressure from the north. The Scandinavia of the eighth and ninth centuries was carrying population growth and pressure on the land, and the Viking expeditions were turning from scattered plunder into organised settlement; and after England had been defeated in 877 and 878 by the army of Alfred and his fellow kings, the English bases and the channels of profit were cut off, the surviving war bands were pushed westward across the sea, and Ireland was the nearest stepping-stone they could find. The invasion of 914 was therefore not an isolated raid but a redeployment after the expulsion from England. The third layer is the structural weakness inside Ireland. The island had no central army, the petty kings obeyed the High King only in name, men and equipment were each region's own business, and an improvised muster could take weeks to complete. The authority of the High King had to be maintained by shared victories, and a single defeat weakened his power to summon. The Vikings exploited exactly this gap in time: they struck while the Irish were still mustering, and left when the business was done. The fourth layer is geography. Dubh Linn, at the mouth of the Liffey, was the one natural anchorage on the eastern coast of Ireland that was sheltered and also commanded the shipping lanes of the Irish Sea. Holding it gave the Vikings a base on which they could levy a return year after year, and every overseas tie of Ireland, in Church, trade and books, passed through these waters. Taking Dubh Linn was therefore a goal both sides knew was worth the cost.
impact:
這場戰爭留下的東西，比它的勝負更持久。
第一，都柏林從Dubh Linn的漁村變成北歐城市網絡中的一個真實城市。920年之後，Sigtrygg在原址重建並加固城防，築起帶城樓的石造城牆，設立定期市集與作坊，並在十世紀鑄造自己的錢幣；十一世紀的考古層顯示城內有木骨泥牆的長屋、鍛鐵作坊、陶窯與禮拜堂，以及石造城牆與城樓的基址。它後來成為王國的首都，維持到十二世紀末被盎格魯—諾曼人攻破為止，歷時約一百五十年。學者把都柏林列為「早期北歐城市」最常引用的實例之一。
第二，愛爾蘭的防禦體系被戰爭改寫。十世紀起，愛爾蘭修道院大量興建石造圓塔——圓形的窄窗塔樓，底層厚重、上層不設窗——用來收藏聖物與鐘鈴，並在圍城時作為避難處。克朗納德的圓塔正是此類。從此愛爾蘭的修院不再只是禱告場所，而是有城牆、有塔、有武裝衛兵的堡壘。
第三，戰爭推動了愛爾蘭的書寫與記錄。愛爾蘭編年史系統記下914至920年的逐年戰況，成為研究中世紀早期愛爾蘭最核心的史料；同一時期抄成的聖加爾普里西安抄本保存了現存最古老的古愛爾蘭語文本。
第四，北歐人在愛爾蘭留下了持久的定居點與網絡：都柏林的商船定期往返英格蘭與曼島；同一個北歐政治圈裡，Sigtrygg的兒子奧拉夫・庫蘭既是都柏林王也是約克王，馬格努斯「赤足」在1090年代末一度奪取都柏林——都柏林從此是北海世界的一枚節點，而不是愛爾蘭的邊境。
第五，軍事上，愛爾蘭人學會了用聯軍集結與選地作戰對付游擊式的敵人，維京人則學會了「不求殲滅、求據點」的長期策略；兩套邏輯在此後百餘年的愛爾蘭—諾斯衝突中一直沿用。
impactEn: What this war left behind is more durable than its outcome. First, Dublin became a real city in the network of northern cities, from what had been the fishing settlement of Dubh Linn. After 920 Sigtrygg rebuilt and strengthened the defences on the old site, raised a stone curtain wall with towers, established periodic markets and workshops, and struck his own coin in the tenth century; the eleventh-century levels show longhouses of timber and clay, an ironworking shop, a kiln and a chapel inside the walls, together with the footings of the stone wall and its towers. It became the capital of the kingdom and held that position until it was taken by the Anglo-Normans at the end of the twelfth century, a run of some hundred and fifty years, and scholars cite Dublin as one of the most frequently used examples of an early northern city. Second, the war rewrote the defensive system of Ireland. From the tenth century the Irish monasteries built stone round towers in great numbers, circular structures with narrow windows, thick at the base and windowless above, used to hold the relics and the bell and to serve as a place of refuge in a siege; the round tower at Clonard is of this kind. The Irish monastery was from then on not merely a place of prayer but a fortification, with walls, a tower and armed guards. Third, the war pushed forward Irish writing and record-keeping. The Irish annals set down the course of the war year by year from 914 to 920 and became the central source for the study of early medieval Ireland, while the St Gall Priscian, copied in the same period, preserves the oldest surviving text in Old Irish. Fourth, the Northmen left a lasting settlement and a network in Ireland: the ships of Dublin ran regularly to England and to the Isles, and within the same northern political circle Sigtrygg's son Amlaíb Cuarán was king of Dublin and of York alike, while Magnus Barefoot seized Dublin once in the late 1090s. From then on Dublin was a node of the North Sea world and not a frontier of Ireland. Fifth, in military terms the Irish learned to meet a skirmishing enemy with a combined muster and a chosen ground, while the Vikings learned the long strategy of seeking a base rather than the destruction of an enemy; both logics were used again in the Irish-Norse conflicts of the following century and more.
result:
920年的決戰之後，這場大規模入侵結束了。愛爾蘭人在利費河畔的戰鬥中擊潰伊瑪的大軍，Dubh Linn的城與泊在河口的船隊一同燒毀，殘餘船隻帶著人退回北海；編年史記「Dubh Linn被焚」，火是撤退時自焚還是愛爾蘭人所放，各家解讀不一，但可以確定的是，維京人在這場戰爭中投入的最大一支軍隊沒有回來。愛爾蘭換來約八十年的相對安寧，直到十一世紀中葉諾斯人捲土重來，1049至1054年間、1070年代與1080年代，圍攻都柏林與基爾代爾的戰事再起。
但北歐人的事業並沒有就此結束。Dubh Linn在戰後仍由諾斯人社群重建，918年之後由Sigtrygg執政的都柏林王國延續了一個半世紀，直到十二世紀末被盎格魯—諾曼人所奪；都柏林在這段時期是北歐城市的模範之一，其市集、鑄幣、鐵器與航運網絡的規模，遠超同時期的愛爾蘭本土城市。愛爾蘭與北歐的關係從此不再只是掠奪與反掠奪，而是穩定存在於同一個互通網絡裡的不同位置：一邊是修道院與鄉村信仰秩序，一邊是河口的商埠與城堡。
就這場戰爭本身而言，結果可以這樣總結：北歐人贏得了Dubh Linn這個位置，愛爾蘭人贏得了914年那一支大軍；雙方都沒有被徹底清出局。卡面hoplite所代表的方陣思想，在這裡走完了一條極長的弧線——它在公元前五世紀的希臘是職業步兵的制式裝備，在914年的Dubh Linn城下，它只剩下「盾牌接在一起時正面比個人結實」這一條原理，仍然決定著會戰的勝負。
resultEn: After the decisive action of 920 the great invasion was over. The Irish broke Ímar's host in the fighting by the Liffey, the town of Dubh Linn and the fleet lying off the river were burned together, and the surviving ships carried men back to the North Sea. The annals record that Dublin was burned; whether the fire was the Vikings' own as they withdrew or the Irish's is read differently by different hands, but what is certain is that the largest host the Vikings had put into this war did not come back. Ireland bought some eighty years of relative quiet, until the Northmen came back in the middle of the eleventh century and the sieges of Dublin and Kildare were fought afresh in 1049-1054, in the 1070s and in the 1080s. The northern enterprise, however, did not end there. Dubh Linn was rebuilt after the war by its Norse community, and the kingdom of Dublin under Sigtrygg from 918 ran for a century and a half until it was taken by the Anglo-Normans at the end of the twelfth century; in that period Dublin was a model northern city, and the scale of its market, its coinage, its ironwork and its shipping network was far beyond that of the Irish cities of the same age. The relation between Ireland and the North ceased to be simply plunder and resistance, and became a fixed set of different positions inside one network of mutual traffic: on one side the monasteries and the rural order of belief, on the other the trading port and the castle at the mouth of the river. As for the war itself, the result can be put this way. The Northmen won the position of Dubh Linn; the Irish won the host of 914. Neither side was completely cleared off the board. And the idea of the phalanx that the hoplite on the card stands for has here run the whole length of a very long arc: in the Greek world of the fifth century BC it was the regulation equipment of a professional infantryman, and below the walls of Dubh Linn in 914 it retained only the single principle that shields locked together make a front stronger than any one man, and that principle still decided the issue of the battle.
